title: fractalwright: books, Mac host and what to build next

questions.title: Books to get
questions.question: Which of these two books should I get for fractalwright?
questions.background: The build plan has a books step. Two titles are still missing from your disk: Peitgen, Juergens and Saupe, 'Chaos and Fractals: New Frontiers of Science' (the standard textbook, about 900 pages), and Mumford, Series and Wright, 'Indra's Pearls' (the source for Kleinian group limit sets; fw.py kleinian already draws them but the recipe has not been checked against the book). Neither is free online. Buying a book is your call.
questions.why: A book on disk gets read and turned into tested rules for the skill. Without it, the Kleinian check and the Peitgen distillation stay open.

guess.why: It checks code that already ships; Peitgen mostly confirms things the research already covers.

questions.title: Mac ComfyUI host
questions.question: Should fractalwright send AI passes to the Mac ComfyUI as well as the PC?
questions.background: fw.py reads its ComfyUI hosts from the FW_COMFY_HOSTS environment variable. The default is the PC only. Adding the Mac means setting FW_COMFY_HOSTS=127.0.0.1:8199,192.168.86.100:8188 permanently with setx, which the permission check blocked last session. AI styling is now off unless you pass --ai, so this only matters when you ask for AI.
questions.why: Yes: I set the variable (you may need to allow it). No: AI passes run on the PC only.

guess.why: AI is opt-in now and rarely used, so a second host saves little.

questions.title: What to build next
questions.question: Which of the remaining fractalwright items matter most to you, in order?
questions.background: v0.2.2 is out with every step done. What's left are improvements: (1) deep zoom on the GPU in the browser page (today deep zoom runs on the CPU, slowly); (2) path-traced 3D renders (more realistic light, minutes per frame); (3) turning 3D fractals into printable meshes through polywright-print; (4) small correctness checks (symmetric-icon and multi-scroll attractor parameters checked against primary papers).
questions.why: I work through the list in your order. Without an answer I follow the guess.

options.label: GPU deep zoom in the browser

guess.why: Deep zooms are the most-watched fractal videos and the CPU path is the slowest part of the plugin.

questions.title: Heavy worth test
questions.question: Should I run the heavy evergreen-worth test on fractalwright (with and without the skill, measured)?
questions.background: The quick worth check came back UNPROVEN, leaning KEEP. The heavy test runs paired sessions with and without the skill and measures the difference. It costs a fair amount of tokens (tens of subagent runs) but no GPU time.
questions.why: It decides KEEP, TRIM or CUT on evidence instead of a lean.

guess.why: Every other released plugin got a measured verdict.
